preamble: The clue for 11 across is normal, with a normal solution to be entered in the grid normally. All other clues consist of two cryptic clues, side by side. The two solutions they generate are to be entered side by side in the grid but cyclically, starting anywhere in the designated space. The required starting points will be confirmed by crossing letters and by the fact that, in the 26 squares around the perimeter of the grid, all the letters A to Z appear once.

clue.text: Horsey type mostly speaking up in ambiguous high voice, which is to shake after losing heart

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the horse-family word is dropped

parts.note: an equid is any member of the horse family
vocal means outspoken

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the shaking word goes

parts.note: to tremble is to shake

explanation.surface: A horsy person, speaking up in a quavering falsetto, shivers nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horsey type mostly speaking up in ambiguous' gives EQUIVOCAL; the rest gives TREBLE. The pair is entered cyclically.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivocal means open to two interpretations; a treble is a boy's soprano voice.

clue.text: Three months in US accommodation fizzle out, I heard, after rest nursing unknown ocular trouble

parts.note: the pronoun, sounding like the organ of sight

explanation.surface: An autumn let falls through, and a tired eye problem follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three months in US accommodation fizzle out' gives FALL FLAT; the rest gives LAZY EYE. The pair is entered cyclically.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall flat is to fail to impress; lazy eye is amblyopia, poor vision in one eye.

clue.text: Deny Ovid was exchanging notes? I didn't hear that, to an extent

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deny Ovid was exchanging' gives DISAVOW; the rest gives SOMEWHAT. The pair is entered cyclically.
explanation.definitionFit: To disavow is to disown or repudiate; somewhat means in some degree, rather.

clue.text: Best mince as bad and vile meat's less prudent

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: 'It's best to' means it is advisable to; rasher is also the comparative of rash, meaning more reckless.

clue.text: Old lady with disrespectful laugh about nurses treated older trouble in fabulous place

taken as written

the numeral one, written as I
